name: Campillo de Llerena – Civil War Museum & Italian cemetery
story: Campillo de Llerena lay just behind the Nationalist line on the static southern Extremadura front. In 1937 Italian units of the mixed Italo-Spanish 'Flechas Azules' brigade, based here, created a war cemetery for their dead. The restored Cementerio de los Italianos and the town's Civil War museum — Extremadura's first — form one complex. The museum, expanded in 2023, recreates a trench and bunker and displays material from the fortifications of south-eastern Badajoz, explaining life in the trenches on both sides. It is presented as a place of remembrance for victims of both sides.
see: The walled Italian cemetery outside the village; in town (Plaza Cívica 1) the museum with a reconstructed trench and bunker and finds from the front.
plan: The museum website recently stated it was closed for renovation — phone the town hall (924 770 131) before travelling. The cemetery is about 1.3 km north of the village centre.
